scope.name: Greater Abu Dhabi City — focused UDES v2 study area
excluded: Outer Abu Dhabi Region districts outside the selected metropolitan study area
scope.note: This is a selected urban system, not the full Abu Dhabi Region. Main-island neighborhoods remain distinct.

classifications.observed: Published directly by the cited government source.
classifications.derived: Calculated from observed geometry, stops or an OSM route snapshot.
classifications.synthetic: Transparent modeling assumption requiring calibration before policy use.
classifications.derived-from-observed: Calculated solely from cited observed records.

adsdiCommunities.title: AD-SDI Open Data — Community
adsdiCommunities.publisher: Department of Government Enablement, Abu Dhabi Spatial Data Infrastructure
adsdiCommunities.use: Official community polygons grouped by official district ID into model zones

adsdiRoadCenterline.title: AD-SDI Open Data — RoadCenterline
adsdiRoadCenterline.publisher: Department of Government Enablement, Abu Dhabi Spatial Data Infrastructure
adsdiRoadCenterline.use: Inspected as the preferred road source; not embedded because the layer is a dense, non-routable centerline inventory

adsdiBusStops.title: AD-SDI Open Data — Bus Stops
adsdiBusStops.publisher: Department of Government Enablement, Abu Dhabi Spatial Data Infrastructure
adsdiBusStops.use: Official stop IDs, names and locations

scadPopulation.title: Abu Dhabi Census — Population 2024
scadPopulation.use: Abu Dhabi Region total and officially disclosed top-ten district populations

unHabitatMobility.title: National Urban Policy Transport Guide — Figure 21
unHabitatMobility.use: Historical Abu Dhabi all-trip mode shares used as a broad calibration check, not a current commute forecast

osm.title: OpenStreetMap
osm.use: Routable road geometry where the official centerline service is impractical

osrm.title: OSRM public routing service
osrm.use: Static shortest-road corridor geometry and free-flow route duration over OpenStreetMap

historicalAllTripModeShareReference.caveat: Historical all-trip shares are used only to reject implausible synthetic model outputs; the model represents work trips and requires a current household travel survey for validation.

calibration.note: Only six selected districts appear in SCAD's published 2024 top-ten values. Other district populations and all district jobs/behavioral attributes are explicitly synthetic baselines.

zones.name: Al Manhal / Al Karamah
zones.mappingNote: Official Al Manhal polygon used for the combined familiar-area label.

zones.name: Muroor / Al Sa'adah
zones.mappingNote: Muroor is a familiar corridor-area rather than an AD-SDI district; official Al Sa'adah is used as the reproducible fallback polygon.

zones.name: Al Reem Island
zones.mappingNote: Official Al Reem Island and Al Reem East Island polygons combined.

zones.name: Rabdan / Al Maqta
zones.mappingNote: Official Rabdan polygon used for the Rabdan / Al Maqta gateway zone.

zones.name: Mohamed Bin Zayed / Zayed City
zones.mappingNote: Two official district polygons combined; only the Mohamed Bin Zayed City population is disclosed in SCAD's 2024 top-ten chart.

officialCenterlineAssessment.reason: The official layer is a dense inventory without turn restrictions or a ready navigable topology; embedding it would be disproportionate for a browser model. Static OSM/OSRM corridors are used instead.

transit.caveat: Stops are observed. Links, frequency, capacity and travel time are modeled because an official route/timetable layer was not available in the AD-SDI open service.

assumptions: Population values for Al Danah, Al Zahiyah, Al Nahyan, Khalifa City, Musaffah and the Mohamed Bin Zayed City component are observed SCAD 2024 top-ten figures.
Other selected-zone population values distribute a plausible metropolitan subtotal but are not official district estimates.
Jobs, capacities, quality, rent indices, car ownership, salaries and employment themes are synthetic starting values, not forecasts or administrative statistics.
Mode-choice parameters are synthetic and checked only against a historical 2015 all-trip reference reported by UN-Habitat/UITP; they are not a current household-travel-survey calibration.
Same-zone mode shares, the 45-day commute escalation grace period and financial car-disposal guards are transparent synthetic work-trip calibration choices.
Muroor uses the official Al Sa'adah polygon; Al Manhal represents the combined Al Manhal / Al Karamah label; Rabdan represents Rabdan / Al Maqta.
Road and transit links are aggregate zone connectors, not a segment-level assignment network.
Each zone centroid is a hand-selected representative activity/network anchor; geometryCentroid is calculated from its official grouped community polygons.
All OSM-derived geometry requires visible OpenStreetMap attribution in the UI.
